hedges.reason: A Russia–Ukraine ceasefire is the most direct instrument for the settlement branch of my failure narrative. If a negotiated Ukrainian withdrawal from the rest of Donetsk is what hands Russia Kostyantynivka, that same deal is a mutually agreed halt to fighting, so this contract pays in exactly the world where my NO basket loses. No listed instrument covers TTF gas, the ruble or European construction names, so this is the closest available expression of 'the war is being settled on Russian terms'.

Official Russia–Ukraine diplomatic meetings are the first step of any settlement. They are also the likely reaction to a front collapse that forces talks, which covers the second failure branch too. It is a lower bar than a ceasefire, so it should pay in more of the worlds where the city falls quickly.

A Trump–Putin summit is how a Russian-terms settlement would be sealed or pushed forward. A fast Russian gain around Kostyantynivka strengthens Moscow's leverage and gives Washington a reason to press for a deal in person.

claims.reason: Going from partial infiltration to ISW shading the entire municipality in about a month is very unlikely through grinding urban combat alone. The plausible route is an agreed Ukrainian withdrawal as part of a deal, and a deal that transfers ground in Donetsk comes with a mutually agreed suspension of fighting.

Both paths to a full capture by year-end lead to direct official contact between Russia and Ukraine. A negotiated handover needs negotiators in the room. A collapse of the Kostyantynivka defense and the threat to Kramatorsk–Sloviansk would push Kyiv to open talks to stop further losses.
